tool_arguments.query: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI remaining performance obligations RPO fiscal 2025 quarter ended May 2025

events.content: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI remaining performance obligations RPO fiscal 2025 quarter ended May 2025

Oracle reported **$138 billion of total remaining performance obligations (RPO)** at the end of fiscal Q4 2025, the quarter ended **May 31, 2025**—an increase of **41% year over year**. [[1]] 

OCI is not disclosed with a standalone RPO balance in Oracle’s earnings release; however, Oracle’s cloud RPO grew **56% year over year** and represented nearly **80% of total RPO**, implying that cloud commitments were the principal driver of the $138 billion backlog. [[2]] 

For context, OCI/IaaS revenue was **$3.0 billion** in the May 2025 quarter, up **52% year over year**. [[1]]

[S2.1] Oracle - Oracle Announces Fiscal 2025 Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Full Year Financial Results — https://investor.oracle.com/investor-news/news-details/2025/Oracle-Announces-Fiscal-2025-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Full-Year-Financial-Results/default.aspx

events.content: Oracle OCI AI revenue growth fiscal 2025 quarter May 2025

For Oracle’s fiscal Q4 2025—the quarter ended May 31, 2025—OCI consumption revenue grew **62% year over year**; Oracle did not separately disclose an “AI revenue” dollar amount or a standalone AI-revenue growth rate in its earnings release. [[1]] 

The broader OCI/IaaS revenue measure was **$3.0 billion, up 52% year over year**, while combined cloud revenue (IaaS plus SaaS) was **$6.7 billion, up 27%**. [[2]] 

Management attributed the OCI demand acceleration to AI-related workloads and said it expected OCI consumption growth to accelerate further in fiscal 2026. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: remaining performance obligations RPO definition conversion to revenue SaaS cloud contracts

events.content: remaining performance obligations RPO definition conversion to revenue SaaS cloud contracts

**Remaining performance obligations (RPO)** are the portion of the transaction price in signed customer contracts that has not yet been recognized as revenue. In SaaS, total RPO generally equals **deferred revenue**—amounts already invoiced or collected but not yet earned—plus **non-cancelable contracted amounts that have not yet been invoiced**. [[1]]

**How RPO converts to SaaS revenue:** 
1. A customer signs a subscription contract, creating a contractual commitment; the unrecognized portion enters RPO. [[1]] 
2. If the customer is billed in advance, the billed amount is initially recorded as a contract liability/deferred revenue rather than revenue. [[2]] 
3. As the company provides continuous access to the hosted software, it satisfies the SaaS performance obligation over the subscription term and recognizes revenue, commonly on a straight-line/rata basis if service is provided evenly. ASC 606 requires recognition when or as the performance obligation is satisfied, and SaaS access is commonly recognized over time because the customer receives the benefit throughout the service period. [[3]] 
4. Each period’s recognized revenue reduces RPO; RPO reaches zero when the remaining contractual services have been delivered, absent a renewal, expansion, or amendment. [[4]]

**Illustration:** A $120,000 non-cancelable 12-month SaaS subscription signed and billed upfront begins with $120,000 of RPO and deferred revenue. If access is provided evenly and there are no other performance obligations, the vendor recognizes $10,000 of revenue per month; after three months, cumulative revenue is $30,000 and remaining RPO is $90,000. The calculation follows the over-time SaaS revenue-recognition principle. [[3]] [[4]]

**Current RPO (cRPO)** is the subset expected to be recognized during the next 12 months; the remainder is expected to convert to revenue after 12 months. For example, a SaaS filer described RPO as deferred revenue plus non-cancelable future billings and separately disclosed the amount expected to be recognized in the following 12 months. [[1]]

**Important analytical distinction:** RPO is not equivalent to next-quarter or next-year revenue, ARR, bookings, or cash collections. It is a contractual revenue backlog measure whose conversion timing depends on contract duration, delivery pattern, renewal/expansion activity, variable-consideration treatment, and any disclosure exemptions for contracts with original terms of one year or less. [[1]] [[2]]

Sources:
[S5.1] Sec — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1393052/000156459019021933/R16.htm
[S5.2] 10-Q — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/935036/000119312518159049/d556994d10q.htm
[S5.3] Performance Obligations Under ASC 606: A Practical Guide — https://jumpstartpartners.finance/blog/performance-obligations
[S5.4] RPOs Explained: SaaS Backlog, ASC 606 & Investor Reporting — https://ordwaylabs.com/blog/metrics-blog/remaining-performance-obligations/
